one_liner: Cloud phone platform for business calls, SMS, and AI voice agents
blocker: API keys are generated inside an Aircall customer account and no free developer tier is documented; OAuth for multi-customer apps additionally requires an approved tech-partner application.

evidence.claim: The public REST API supports two auth methods: Basic Authentication (API ID + token, Base64) and OAuth 2.0
evidence.quote: Aircall supports two ways to authenticate with the REST API: Basic Authentication and OAuth.

evidence.claim: Basic-auth API keys require an Aircall customer account and are generated self-serve from the dashboard (Integrations > API keys)
evidence.quote: You must have an Aircall account. Sign up as a customer here

evidence.claim: OAuth credentials for public/multi-customer apps are gated behind an approved tech-partner application
evidence.quote: If approved, you'll receive your developer account and OAuth credentials to start building

evidence.claim: API surface is broad: reference lists 9+ object groups (Users V1/V2, Teams, Calls, Dialer, Numbers, Conversation Intelligence, Messages, Contacts, Tags, Webhooks); Calls alone has 10+ operations
evidence.quote:

evidence.claim: Aircall's official developer platform documents MCP as a first-class capability for connecting tools to its AI Virtual Agents
evidence.quote: Connect your tools and data to Aircall's AI Virtual Agents through MCP.

notes: MCP caveat: Aircall's docs position MCP as a way to plug YOUR tools/MCP servers into Aircall's AI Virtual Agents (Aircall acts as MCP client), not a vendor-hosted MCP server exposing the Aircall API; unofficial third-party MCP servers exist (@allo/aircall-mcp-server with 73 tools, CassiaResearch with 83 tools) but are not vendor-official. OAuth is account-level: one access_token per account, admin selects which phone numbers the app can access, users matched by email. Whether a free trial yields API keys is not stated in the supplied material, so access is classed as paid_plan_required. Docs offer an llms.txt index, webhooks, WhatsApp messaging endpoints, and an official Postman collection.
